overview: The two lipoproteins most discussed in cardiovascular risk, distinguished by density, composition, and the direction they carry cholesterol.
genZNote: HDL cleans up. LDL drops stuff off (sometimes where it shouldn't).

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A lipoprotein that transports excess cholesterol from peripheral tissues back to the liver for excretion — "good" cholesterol carrier.
aspects.valueB: A lipoprotein that transports cholesterol from the liver to peripheral tissues — "bad" cholesterol carrier when in excess.

aspects.label: Density and Composition
aspects.valueA: High protein-to-lipid ratio, making it denser.
aspects.valueB: Higher lipid-to-protein ratio, making it less dense.

aspects.label: Direction of Cholesterol Transport
aspects.valueA: Reverse cholesterol transport — tissues to liver.

aspects.label: Clinical Association
aspects.valueA: Higher levels generally associated with lower cardiovascular risk.
aspects.valueB: Elevated levels associated with atherosclerosis and increased cardiovascular risk.

aspects.label: Laboratory Measurement
aspects.valueA: Measured directly or calculated as part of a standard lipid panel.
aspects.valueB: Often calculated using the Friedewald equation from total cholesterol, HDL, and triglycerides.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Delivers cholesterol to tissues; "bad" cholesterol in excess.
